_comment: Claude Code hooks template. Drop into .claude/hooks/hooks.json in the consumer's repo (or runtimes/.claude/hooks/hooks.json for SpecForge's own runtime template). Each top-level key is a trigger type (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse). Each entry has an optional 'matcher' (tool name or regex) and a list of hooks (commands to execute).

_trigger_reference.SessionStart: Fires once when a session begins. Use for: status banners, environment checks, orientation. Cannot block (informational only).
_trigger_reference.PreToolUse: Fires before any tool invocation that matches 'matcher'. Use for: validation gates, blocking unsafe operations. Exit non-zero to block; stderr is shown to the user.
_trigger_reference.PostToolUse: Fires after a tool completes. Use for: validation, lint, follow-up actions. Cannot block (the action already happened); use stderr for warnings.

_matcher_reference._: Empty string matches all invocations of the trigger.

_protocol.stdin: Hook scripts receive a JSON object on stdin: { 'tool_input': { ... }, ... }. Parse with python3 or jq.

exit_codes.non_zero: Block (PreToolUse only). PostToolUse and SessionStart hooks cannot block - non-zero is treated as informational.

_protocol.stderr: Anything written to stderr is shown to the user. Use for actionable messages.

_anti_patterns: Don't run slow operations in hooks. Sub-second target.
Don't ask the user questions in a hook - hooks can't be interactive. Use a skill.
Don't make hooks non-idempotent. They fire on every event.
Don't skip exit-code discipline. Failing closed is the safe default for PreToolUse.
_reference_implementations: See .claude/hooks/ at the repo root for working hooks: session-start-status.sh (banner), pre-bash-sanitize.sh (sanitization gate on git commit), post-edit-frontmatter.sh (frontmatter validation on agent/skill writes).
